scene_summary: A small office with a blind-covered window, low wooden cubby shelf, two gray swivel chairs, a dark desk, floor lamp, paneled door and plant.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction recovers most major objects and their broad arrangement, but the framing and visible floor area differ, the door appears much smaller and more slab-like, and the floor and desk materials lack the reference's darker textured appearance. The foreground chair and plant are also substantially differently framed.

main_defects.description: The view is wider and more elevated, placing the furniture smaller in frame and cropping the desk and plant differently. The foreground chair is displaced toward the right edge rather than centered in the room.
main_defects.evidence: The reference desk dominates the lower left, the front chair is near the lower center, and the plant's pot is visible; the reconstruction shows a broad desk edge, a chair at the right, and mostly plant blades.
main_defects.uncertainty: Camera viewpoint, object placement, and object scale can all contribute to these differences.

main_defects.description: The door is noticeably narrower and shorter in the image and reads as a freestanding thick slab rather than the large door occupying much of the right wall in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference door reaches near the top of the frame and has a broad visible face; the reconstruction door is lower, narrower and has an obvious thick side face.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent size difference may result from the camera and perspective rather than physical dimensions.

main_defects.description: The reference's brown, visibly grained plank flooring is replaced by pale, nearly uniform tiles or planks; the desk is also lighter and flatter in appearance.
main_defects.evidence: Dark wood grain and varied brown tones cover much of the reference floor, whereas the reconstruction floor is light gray with simple seams and little surface variation.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may account for part of the color difference.

main_defects.description: The foreground chair does not visibly reproduce the reference's prominent black central support and five-spoke caster base.
main_defects.evidence: The reference foreground chair has a clearly exposed black post and wheeled base; in the reconstruction only its shell is clearly visible above the foreground desk and plant.
main_defects.uncertainty: The base may be present but hidden by the desk, plant, or framing.

main_defects.description: The window and shelf appear smaller and less visually dominant, and the blind has conspicuous dark corner fasteners absent from the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference window is large and framed in pale wood, with a wide cubby shelf below; the reconstruction's window and shelf occupy a smaller portion of the view and black spots appear at the blind corners.
main_defects.uncertainty: The apparent proportions are affected by the changed camera viewpoint.

strengths: The major office objects are recognizable and broadly arranged in the same room: blind and cubby shelf on the left wall, door on the right, chairs in front, floor lamp to the left, and plant in the foreground.
The pale walls, wooden shelf, horizontal blind slats, gray chair shells, and paneled dark door capture important visual features of the reference.
The central chair has a visible black wheeled swivel base and the shelf has multiple open cubbies.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Different camera framing and occlusion make it difficult to distinguish geometry and placement errors from viewpoint effects; hidden objects or parts are not assumed absent.
